title: High-Throughput Kinase Activity Mapping \(HT-KAM) system: biochemical assay
protocol: Place 10 cm petri dish on ice where cells are cultured.
Wash cells profusely three times with cold PBS, keeping cell culture dishes on ice and vacuum-sucking the extra volume of PBS at the last wash.
Add between 750 μL and 1.5 mL of freshly prepared, cold Cell Lysis Buffer to the petri dish.
Scrape cells using a regular flat tip scraper while maintaining them on ice.
Tilt the petri dish and leave for 5 min with cell suspension in lysis buffer/inhibitor cocktail (keep on ice).
Collect cell lysates in eppendorf centrifuge tubes.
Spin for 15 minutes at 14,000 rpm at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant into a new tube without collecting any pelleted debris and aliquot 50 to 100 μL per eppendorf.
Flash-freeze resected tissue and store at -80°C until use.
On the day of protein extraction, pulverize flash-frozen tissues while keeping them on ice and collect in tubes.
Add between 750 μL and 1.5 mL of freshly prepared cold Cell Lysis Buffer to the pulverized tissue and follow subsequent steps as detailed for cultured cells.
Use a liquid dispensing instrument to aliquot peptide + sample + ATP + buffer solutions in 384-well plates.
Keep all reagents on ice until enzymatic reactions are started.
Automate the dispensing of an 8 μL reaction mixture per well in 384-well plates, containing kinase assay buffer, 250 nM ATP, 200 μg/mL 11-mer peptide, and samples.
Maintain all 384-well plates on cold blocks during dispensing steps.
Incubate the 384-well plates for 30 minutes at 30°C after dispensing is completed.
Dispense Kinase-Glo revealing reagent using an automated liquid dispensing instrument after enzymatic reactions are completed.
Measure luminescence using Synergy 2 Multi-Mode Microplate Reader from BioTek.
